_comment: Human-curated seed data for the knowledge graph. Edit here, then re-run npm run data:kg.

orders.name: Chishtiyya
orders.description: One of the most prominent Sufi orders of South Asia, founded by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti. Emphasises love, tolerance, and music (sama).
orders.descriptionUr: برصغیر کے نمایاں ترین صوفی سلسلوں میں سے ایک، جس کی بنیاد خواجہ معین الدین چشتی نے رکھی۔ محبت، رواداری اور سماع پر زور دیتا ہے۔

orders.name: Suhrawardiyya
orders.description: Order founded by Diya ud-Din Abu'n-Najib al-Suhrawardi; became dominant in Multan and Sindh under Bahauddin Zakariya.
orders.descriptionUr: یہ سلسلہ ضیاء الدین ابو النجیب سہروردی سے منسوب ہے؛ بہاؤالدین زکریا کے زمانے میں ملتان اور سندھ میں غالب رہا۔

orders.name: Qadiriyya
orders.description: Order tracing to Abd al-Qadir Gilani of Baghdad; arrived in South Asia via multiple chains; strong presence in Punjab.
orders.descriptionUr: یہ سلسلہ بغداد کے شیخ عبدالقادر جیلانی سے جا ملتا ہے؛ برصغیر میں کئی سندوں کے ذریعے پہنچا؛ پنجاب میں اس کی موجودگی مضبوط ہے۔

orders.name: Qalandariyya
orders.description: Antinomian Sufi tradition named after the qalandars; characterised by wandering, intoxication of divine love, and freedom from formal religious observance.
orders.descriptionUr: قلندروں سے منسوب ایک آزاد رَو صوفی روایت؛ اس کی پہچان سفر، عشقِ الٰہی کی سرمستی اور رسمی مذہبی پابندیوں سے بے نیازی ہے۔

orders.name: Naqshbandiyya
orders.description: Order tracing to Baha ud-Din Naqshband Bukhari; emphasises silent dhikr and close adherence to shari'a.
orders.descriptionUr: یہ سلسلہ بہاؤالدین نقشبند بخاری سے جا ملتا ہے؛ ذکرِ خفی اور شریعت کی سخت پابندی پر زور دیتا ہے۔

orders.name: Rashidi
orders._why: Named by the corpus as "the Rashidi Sufi order", founded by Pir Muhammad Rashid Shah himself. No parent order: the same row separately calls him "A Qadiri-Naqshbandi saint" but does not say the Rashidi is a branch of either, so none is asserted.

orders.name: Malamati
orders._why: The silsila cell on Shah Hussain's row, verbatim. The prose calls the current "the Malamatiyya", "the Sufis of the 'path of blame'"; the slug follows the sheet's form because a sheet value is a join key (RULE 3). No parent order is named anywhere.

orders.name: Azeemia
orders._why: The silsila cell on Qalandar Baba Auliya's row. A twentieth-century foundation with no parent named; its transmission is given as Qalandar Baba Auliya to Khwaja Shamsuddin Azeemi.

orders.name: Shattari
orders._why: Named as a silsila in its own right, on a par with the Qadiri, in the one sentence describing Shah Inayat's practice: "He combined the Qadiri and Shattari silsilas in his own practice." A parent-level order in the source, not a Qadiri sub-branch, even though the recorded cell fuses the two as "Qadri Shattari".

saintOrders.comment: Keys must match the slug generated from the canonical saint name after merge variants are applied.

saintMergeVariants.comment: Maps a raw CSV value to its canonical saint name. Applied before slug generation. Add entries when the same saint appears under multiple name forms.

_comment_saintDoNotMerge: Merges this project has decided AGAINST, each with the corpus sentence that forbids it. saintMergeVariants above says which names are one person; this says which look like one person and are not. It exists because the merge is the destructive direction: on this corpus the figures most likely to share a name are father and son, uncle and nephew, master and disciple, so a similarity merge does not merely mis-name someone — it deletes the edge that made the pair worth recording. A honorific-stripping token matcher run on 28 August 2026 proposed 21 merges here and 19 were wrong; those 19 are the reason most of these rows exist. Enforced by scripts/data/validate-kg-identity.mjs, which fails the build if any pair collapses into one node and re-checks every quote byte-for-byte against its source. Adding a row is cheap and permanent; deleting one needs a reason better than "the names look the same".

saintDoNotMerge.reason: Pupil and master, not one man. `khwaja-muhammad-qasim` is Zinda Pir of Ghamkol Sharif (1912–1999); `khwaja-muhammad-qasim-sadiq` is the founder of Mohra Sharif (b. c. 1846), who granted him khilafat. Merging them deletes the disciple_of edge that is the reason both are recorded.
saintDoNotMerge.quote: from his own guide, Baba Ji Muhammad Qasim of Mohra Sharif

saintDoNotMerge.reason: The entry devotes a section to forbidding this merge. Different centuries, different cities, ~150 km apart; the shared element is the honorific.
saintDoNotMerge.quote: The two are unrelated: different centuries, different cities, and no source treats them as the same figure.

saintDoNotMerge.reason: The Sialkot entry opens by insisting on the distinction. Bari Imam is Syed Abdul Latif Shah Kazmi of Nurpur Shahan; the shared element is the honorific "Imam".
saintDoNotMerge.quote: with whom the similar honorific "Imam" sometimes causes confusion: the figure venerated at Sialkot is a separate personage belonging to the local history of that city

saintDoNotMerge.reason: A honorific-stripping matcher proposed this merge on 28 August 2026 and it is wrong. `shaikh-abdul-latif` is the father and first teacher of Khwaja Muhammad Zaman of Luari Sharif, a Naqshbandi; Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai is the Sindhi poet of the Risalo.
saintDoNotMerge.quote: Muhammad Zaman received his first instruction from his father, Shaikh Abdul Latif, a follower of the Naqshbandi order

saintDoNotMerge.reason: A honorific-stripping matcher proposed this merge and it is wrong. `sayyid-shah-inayat` is the maternal uncle and murshid of Syed Sakhi Shah Chan Charagh in Sindh; Shah Inayat Qadiri is the Lahore master of Bulleh Shah (b. c. 1643, d. c. 1728).

saintDoNotMerge.reason: A honorific-stripping matcher proposed this merge and it is wrong. The shared element is the epithet *Sarmast*. `shah-saidan-sarmast` is the Suhrawardi master of Shah Daula Daryai; Sachal Sarmast is the Sindhi poet of Daraza.
saintDoNotMerge.quote: he became the disciple of a Suhrawardi *faqir* remembered as Shah Saidan Sarmast

saintDoNotMerge.reason: A honorific-stripping matcher proposed this merge and it is wrong. `sayyid-abdul-rahman-of-delhi` is the Qadiri initiator of Sultan Bahu; Rahman Baba is the Pashto poet Abdur Rahman Mohmand of Peshawar. The shared element is the name Rahman.

saintDoNotMerge.reason: A honorific-stripping matcher proposed this merge and it is wrong. `hazrat-hafiz-muhammad-abdur-rahman` is the son and successor of Baba Ji at Eidgah Sharif, Rawalpindi; Rahman Baba is the Pashto poet.
saintDoNotMerge.quote: Upon Baba Ji's death the spiritual seat passed to his son, *Hazrat Hafiz Muhammad Abdur Rahman*

saintDoNotMerge.reason: A honorific-stripping matcher proposed this merge on the shared element "Abdul" alone. `khwaja-abdul-haq` is the uncle and initiator of Sachal Sarmast; `hazrat-syed-abdul-wahab` is Akhund Panju Baba of the Pashtun country under Akbar.

saintDoNotMerge.reason: A honorific-stripping matcher proposed this merge on the shared element "Tahir". `hazrat-syedna-tahir-alauddin-qadiri-gilani` is a twentieth-century Qadiri teacher named among Ganj-e-Inayat Sarkar’s teachers; `sheikh-tahir` is the figure of Odero Lal in Sindh.
saintDoNotMerge.quote: Hazrat Syedna Tahir Alauddin Qadiri Gilani

saintDoNotMerge.reason: A honorific-stripping matcher proposed this merge on the shared element "Ghulam". `maulana-ghulam-ali-okarvi` is an orator named among Ganj-e-Inayat Sarkar’s teachers; Khwaja Ghulam Farid is the Seraiki poet of Kot Mithan.
saintDoNotMerge.quote: the renowned orator Maulana Ghulam Ali Okarvi

saintDoNotMerge.reason: Both are "Abdul Karim" and they are three centuries and a province apart. `hazrat-hafiz-muhammad-abdul-karim` is Baba Ji of Eidgah Sharif, Rawalpindi, whose seat passed to his son Hafiz Muhammad Abdur Rahman; Shah Abdul Karim Bulri is the Sindhi poet of Bulri, forebear of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai. Recorded when the kinship pass added the first as a lineage-only node, because a similarity matcher would join them and both men are in this graph precisely for a father-son edge that the merge would delete.
saintDoNotMerge.quote: Upon Baba Ji's death the spiritual seat passed to his son, *Hazrat Hafiz Muhammad Abdur Rahman*

_comment_saintCompositeFigures: Rows whose figure cell names more than one person, mapped to the figures it names, primary first. Applied instead of saintMergeVariants for these cells, and the reason it has to exist: the schema gives a row one `principal_figure`, but some sites are held by two people and the sheet says so — with a `;` in `principal_figure`, and with "&" or "and" in the legacy cell. Every earlier handling lost one of the two. "Guru Nanak and Bhai Mardana" was a saintMergeVariants entry resolving to "Guru Nanak", which is why Bhai Mardana appeared NOWHERE in this graph; the other two became single nodes named after both people, so Gurdwara Panjvi Chati Patshahi reached neither Guru Arjan Dev’s page nor Guru Hargobind’s. The FIRST name listed is the only one the row’s own figure_type / figure_born / figure_died may describe: Rori Sahib records figure_type "Sikh Guru" and Bhai Mardana was not a Guru, so copying it across would make the graph assert what the sheet never said (RULE 2). build-kg.mjs enforces that, logs a `composite-figure-row` review item, and carries the raw cell onto each `buried_at` edge as `asRecorded`. Only add a row here where the cell genuinely names separate people: a `;` inside a parenthetical is not one (darbar-wasif-ali-wasif), nor is one deity under two names ("Jhulelal / Daryalal"), nor a note about practice ("...; veneration of Guru Nanak").
_comment_saintFigureByShrine: Shrine slug -> the figure that site actually commemorates, overriding the row's `Sufi Saint` cell. Needed because the cell-keyed maps above structurally cannot express this: two rows can carry the BYTE-IDENTICAL legacy cell and be about different people, and saintMergeVariants/saintCompositeFigures are keyed on the cell, so anything they do to one they do to both. Use this ONLY where the sheet itself already contradicts the legacy cell (a differing `principal_figure`, `figure_type` or date columns) — never to assert a figure the sheet is silent about (RULE 2). Each entry is a bridge, not a destination: the real fix is a CSV patch correcting the sheet, and `validate-kg-identity.mjs` check 8 fails an entry once the sheet catches up, so a stale override cannot sit here unnoticed.

tomb-of-javindi-bibi.why: The row's `Sufi Saint` cell reads 'Jalaluddin Surkh-Posh Bukhari' — byte-identical to the cell on 'Shrine of Jalaluddin Surkh-Posh Bukhari', a different monument about a different person — so the graph filed a woman's tomb as one of his two shrines. The sheet already disagrees with itself here in three columns: `principal_figure` is 'Bibi Jawindi', `figure_type` is 'Historical person' where his row says 'Sufi saint', and `figure_born`/`figure_died` (1192/1291) appear only on his row. Nothing is invented by this entry; it adopts what the sheet's own newer columns say. Patch to correct the sheet: data/patch_javindi_bibi_figure_2026-08-28.csv.

_comment_saintDescriptiveCells: Figure cells that are a name PLUS a description, mapped to the name alone. Distinct from saintMergeVariants, which joins spelling variants of one name: these cells are not variants, they are a name with a clause attached — "…, described in the survey as slave of Mahmud Ghaznavi", "…, disciple of Guru Gobind Singh", "…, son of Rama and Sita". slugify() swallowed the clause, so the archive published figure URLs that are whole sentences; malik-ahmad-ayaz's was seventeen words long, and prerender emits a file for each one. The clause is NOT discarded: build-kg keeps the full recorded cell as an altName, so the survey's own wording is still on the figure's page and searchable (RULE 2). Shortening retires a published URL, which retiredSlugs turns into a redirect. Only add a row here where the extra text describes the figure rather than naming them — a longer name is not a description, and 16 of the archive's 21 six-word-plus slugs are simply long names (Shaikh Shihab-ud-Din Abu Hafs Umar al-Suhrawardi) and must be left alone.

saintDescriptiveCells.Hazrat Syed Muhammad Khair ul Deen, know: Hazrat Syed Muhammad Khair ul Deen

_comment_saintDisplayNames: Figure slug -> the name the page should be TITLED with, while the slug itself stays put. Rauf's ruling of 29 August 2026 on the epithet rows: the formal name is the better record and the epithet is what a reader searches for and links to, so the archive keeps both — principal_figure supplies the title, the legacy slug supplies the URL, and the epithet becomes an altName so nothing is lost. This is CLAUDE.md RULE 3 applied literally: a sheet value is a join key and a label is cosmetic, so a better label must never cost a published address. Keyed on the slug rather than on the cell, because the whole point is that the slug does not move. NOT for a row where the two columns name different people, change an honorific class, or turn a person into a collective — three such rows (pir-abdul-ul-karim, guru-gurpat, bibi-pak-daman) were deliberately held out of this ruling and are back in the worksheet unanswered. One thing this quietly fixes: jahaniyan-jahangasht would have become the slug `sayyid-jalaluddin`, one suffix from his grandfather `sayyid-jalaluddin-surkh-posh-bukhari`. Keeping the slug removes the collision that made that row the second place principal_figure was worse. APPLIED TO TWO OF SEVEN so far. The ruling can only be carried out where the formal name exists in URDU: otherwise the English page moves to the formal name and the Urdu page falls back through altNames to the epithet, and the two editions title the same figure differently — which CLAUDE.md's i18n contract forbids and which no gate here would have caught, because the altName fallback keeps the parity test green. Five are waiting on an Urdu name and are listed in _pending_saintDisplayNames; check 9 of validate-kg-identity.mjs fails any entry whose title has no Urdu, so the constraint is now enforced rather than remembered.

_comment_familyRelations: Kinship the archive states in its own prose. 28 edges over 26 rows, every one copied verbatim (name, wording, quote, source) from data/kg-lineage-proposals.json#familyRelations, where an extraction pass recorded them and NOTHING read them: the graph knew only disciple_of and successor_of, so blood and marriage — which is how a gaddi actually passes in this corpus — were held and not rendered. Slugs, kinType and the two role labels are decisions made here by a human; the prose fields are not retyped. Direction is always junior → senior: the subject is the son, grandson, nephew, son-in-law or descendant of the object. `elderRole`/`juniorRole` come from a closed vocabulary because Urdu splits what English does not — a paternal grandfather is دادا and a maternal one نانا — and a label that picks a side the source never states is an invented fact (RULE 2). Where the entry says which line, the specific term is used; where it does not, the *Unspecified role keeps both readings. Two rows in the proposals file record a real family succession and name nobody on the other end; they are in `kinNotes` below, as notes rather than edges, so they are not lost.

familyRelations.notes: The spiritual-heir half of this is already in existing-lineage.json; recorded here only for the blood link, including the intervening father Sadr-ud-Din Arif.
familyRelations._why: The quote states the patriline explicitly — "the grandson of Baha-ud-Din Zakariya and son of Sadr-ud-Din Arif" — so the Urdu may say دادا/پوتا rather than the unspecified pair.

familyRelations.quote: Chief among his descendants was his grandson, Sayyid Jalaluddin known as Makhdoom Jahaniyan Jahangasht
familyRelations.notes: Blood only. Neither entry says the Uch seat passed directly from grandfather to grandson.
familyRelations._why: The entry says "his grandson" and does not say through which parent, so the Urdu keeps both readings.

familyRelations.quote: A separate source, Alam Faqri's *Tazkirah Awliya-e-Pakistan*, instead calls him Bhittai's great-grandfather (three generations, not four)

familyRelations.quote: holds that the six were the daughters of the great saint Sayyid Ahmad Tokhta Tirmidhi, “Murshid-e-Punjab,”

familyRelations._why: Bibi Pak Daman is a `Collective` figure — six women — so the junior role is plural. The entry reports this as one of two competing traditions about who the six were, and the row is marked contested rather than resolved. The role stays singular and `juniorIsPlural` does the pluralising, so there is one mechanism for it and not two.

familyRelations.quote: Upon Baba Ji's death the spiritual seat passed to his son, *Hazrat Hafiz Muhammad Abdur Rahman*
familyRelations.notes: The entry calls the pattern "This unbroken chain of father-to-son succession".
familyRelations._why: The entry calls him "Baba Ji". He is NOT Shah Abdul Karim Bulri, the Sindhi poet’s forebear — see saintDoNotMerge.

familyRelations.quote: his line continues unbroken under his son and successor
it is now held by the latter’s son, Shahid Rasool Shah Gilani Suhrawardi
was succeeded by his son Sai Chanduram
His father's name was Syed Ul Hassan Kabeer. His father was also a pious Sufi and a scholar of Deen (religion).
His father's name was Hazrat Mian Fazal Deen, who himself was a very great scholar of Deen (religion).

familyRelations.subjectName: Sayyid Abul Faiz Qalandar Ali Gilani Suhrawardi
familyRelations.quote: a saint is said to have brought his grandfather, Jamal-ud-Din Gilani, the glad tidings that a grandson would be born in his house
familyRelations._why: "a grandson would be born in his house" suggests the patriline but does not state it, so the Urdu keeps both readings.

_comment_kinNotes: Family the archive records without naming the relative. Not edges — there is no second node to point at — but real recorded facts, shown on the figure’s own page.

kinNotes.wording: succeeded to the seat on his brother's death
kinNotes.quote: his father and, after him, his elder brother were the spiritual guides (*sajjada-nashins*) of their line, and on his brother’s death Ghulam Farid succeeded to the seat
kinNotes.notes: A real succession, but neither the father nor the brother is named, so no edge can be drawn. Recorded here so it is not lost.

kinNotes.quote: it is said to have been raised by the saint's grandson, who is himself buried within the complex
kinNotes.notes: Building patronage by an unnamed grandson; no lineage claim.
